title: runner.conf
description: The keys of a project's runner.conf. The file itself is not JSON: it is one KEY=value per line, sourced by zsh and read by Python, so there are no spaces round the =, no comment after a value, and single quotes round any value holding spaces or symbols. Lists are words separated by spaces. This schema describes the keys as if the file were one JSON object of strings. Lines starting # are comments.

PROJECT.description: The project's name, as the prompts and notices say it.

WORKSPACE.description: Absolute path of the workspace directory. It must be inside a git repository.

REPOS.description: Absolute paths of the code repositories, separated by spaces. A session starts in the first.

PRODUCT_DIRS.description: Caller check: directories (from the repository root, each ending in /) where a new Python function must have a caller. Empty switches the check off.

FREE_DIRS.description: New-file check: directories whose new files need not be named in the task. The workspace's runs/ is always free.

REGISTRY_FILE.description: Optional. A file that registers functions by name; a function listed there counts as called.

LIVE_FLAG_PATTERN.description: Optional. Python regular expression for a line that switches a live write on.

LIVE_FLAG_FILE.description: Optional. The file (path suffix) LIVE_FLAG_PATTERN is looked for in.

NOTIFY.description: How the owner is told: none writes runs/notify.log only; desktop shows a desktop notice; command runs NOTIFY_CMD.

NOTIFY_CMD.description: For NOTIFY=command: a command that receives the message as its one, last argument.

DASHBOARD_URL.description: Optional. The address of a runner dashboard (the kit's dashboard/serve.py) this project's runner reports to. Empty uses the machine's own setting, ~/.config/runner-kit/dashboard.conf, if there is one; off reports to nobody. A dashboard's token is never written in runner.conf.

PREFLIGHT_CMD.description: Optional. A command run before each task; a failure is a warning only.

CHECK_CMD.description: Optional. The project's own check (for example its test suite): one shell command, run from the first repository, that exits 0 when the project is sound. Run by run_task.sh before a task's first session and again on the task's commit. A commit that turns a passing check into a failing one sends the session back to repair it; a check that already fails is reported to the owner once.

STOP_STREAK.description: How many different tasks may stop one after another before the queue pauses and tells the owner. 0 never pauses.

DEFAULT_BUILDER.description: The letter a new task's M column gets by default. The self-test runs its real task with this letter.

DEFAULT_EFFORT.description: The effort word a new task gets by default.

DEFAULT_REVIEWER.description: The R column a new task gets by default: a letter and an effort, or owner.

SUPERVISOR.description: The letter whose adapter and model run a stop session.

CLAUDE_ALLOWED_TOOLS.description: Claude adapter: tools an unattended session may use without asking, as words. Empty relies on the machine's own Claude Code settings.

CLAUDE_MIN_VERSION.description: Claude adapter: optional minimum command-line version.

CLAUDE_TOOLS.description: Claude adapter: the built-in tools a session is given, as words. Every tool's description is re-read on every turn, so a short list is cheaper. Task is the tool that starts the reviewer. Empty gives every tool.

CLAUDE_MCP.description: Claude adapter: no starts sessions without the machine's MCP servers and connectors; yes leaves them as the machine has them.

DEPLOYS.description: Whether the project deploys. yes needs a deploy.sh in the workspace.

LIVE_CHECK_CMD.description: The command that proves what is live: it prints the commit the running system reports as the first word of its output. Used by deploy.sh.

^ADAPTER_[A-Z]$.description: The adapter for a letter: the name of a file in the kit's adapters/ directory, without .sh.

^MODEL_[A-Z]$.description: The exact model id for a letter, as that agent's command-line tool takes it. Pin an id, not an alias. Empty makes the letter unusable.
